cues.zh: 我还要感谢 DraftBit 和 Mike 举办这次活动。你们所做的一切真的太棒了。我非常感激，其他人也一样。

cues.en: Also, thank you to to all of the sponsors that
cues.zh: 同时，感谢所有赞助商，

cues.zh: 感谢你们出资帮助促成了这次活动。

cues.en: So I'm Jordan,
cues.zh: 我是 Jordan，

cues.en: and I'm gonna talk about React and Reason today.
cues.zh: 今天我要讲的是 React 和 Reason。

cues.en: So I work on programming languages and frameworks
cues.zh: 我在 Facebook 的广告界面团队工作，

cues.en: at Facebook on the ads interfaces team.
cues.zh: 从事编程语言和框架方面的工作。

cues.en: And, you know, you you might ask, why do I work on this stuff?
cues.zh: 你可能会问，我为什么要做这些？

cues.en: So my ultimate goal, or at least my personal goal, is to build an application that is fast and that doesn't break when it's extended. And I keep finding that it's just way way too hard to do that.
cues.zh: 我的最终目标，或者说至少是我个人的目标，是构建一个速度快、并且在扩展时不会崩溃的应用。但我一直发现这实在太难做到了。

cues.en: So I end up working on languages and frameworks with the goal of being able to make that job easier, but really, I just wanna use those tools myself.
cues.zh: 所以我转而研究语言和框架，目标是想让这项工作变得更容易，但实际上，我只是想自己用这些工具。

cues.en: And we have a long ways to go. No matter what we do, it always seems like there's
cues.zh: 我们还有很长的路要走。无论我们做什么，似乎总是有

cues.en: there's so much low hanging fruit making the app developers experience better,
cues.zh: 总是有太多容易摘到的果实，可以让应用开发者的体验更好，

cues.en: but we have made some progress.
cues.zh: 但我们已经取得了一些进展。

cues.en: I've been able to participate in some of these projects as well. So in 2011, I created the React JS framework.
cues.zh: 我也参与过其中一些项目。2011 年，我创建了 React JS 框架。

cues.en: Then I shift my focus to mobile where I cofounded the React Native project with three other people.
cues.zh: 然后我把重心转向移动端，与另外三人共同创立了 React Native 项目。

cues.en: And most recently,
cues.zh: 最近，

cues.en: I started the Reason effort and with other coworkers and the community, I helped build out a lot of the tooling that makes up the Reason ecosystem.
cues.zh: 我发起了 Reason 项目，并与其他同事和社区一起，帮助构建了构成 Reason 生态系统的许多工具。

cues.en: So what is Reason?
cues.zh: 那么 Reason 是什么？

cues.en: Reason is a fast and safe programming language based directly on OCaml.
cues.zh: Reason 是一门直接基于 OCaml 的快速且安全的编程语言。

cues.en: So the way I like to think about it is that Reason brings the ideas and the principles that you like about React to the whole language.
cues.zh: 所以我喜欢这样理解：Reason 把你喜欢 React 的那些理念和原则带到了整个语言中。

cues.en: But most importantly,
cues.zh: 但最重要的是，

cues.en: I see it as a way to unlock a much more ambitious future
cues.zh: 我把它看作是一种解锁更宏大未来的方式

cues.en: for UI development.
cues.zh: 为 UI 开发。

cues.en: Alright. So React.
cues.zh: 好，那么说说 React。

cues.en: We open sourced React
cues.zh: 我们在 2013 年
开源了 React

cues.en: and Tom Okino and I presented at JSConf.
cues.zh: 我和 Tom Okino 在 JSConf 上做了演讲。

cues.en: And I haven't really done a lot of conference talk since then,
cues.zh: 从那以后我就没怎么做大会演讲了，

cues.en: but I do go to a lot of meetups.
cues.zh: 但我确实会参加很多聚会。

cues.en: And I talk to a of people and I hear the stories about people adopting React.
cues.zh: 我和很多人交流，听到他们采用 React 的故事。

cues.en: And a lot of the stories have something in common. People say,
cues.zh: 很多故事都有共同点。人们说，

cues.en: React made my job fun again. And I think that's really cool feedback
cues.zh: React 让我的工作重新变得有趣了。我觉得这是很棒的反馈

cues.en: and I try to think about why is that.
cues.zh: 我试着思考为什么会这样。

cues.en: I don't really think it's because React provides like, out of the box IDE integration
cues.zh: 我并不真的认为是因为 React 提供了开箱即用的 IDE 集成

cues.en: and, you know, an abundance of packages that they can just pull down immediately.
cues.zh: 以及大量可以立即拉取的包。

cues.en: Although all that stuff is really great, we should strive for it. I think that something deeper is going on.
cues.zh: 虽然这些东西都很棒，我们应该追求它们。但我认为背后有更深层的东西。

cues.en: I think that React is putting a new idea about how to build apps into people's brains.
cues.zh: 我认为 React 正在把一种构建应用的新理念植入人们的头脑中。

cues.en: And it's that core idea that feels rewarding to people.
cues.zh: 而正是这个核心理念让人们觉得有回报感。

cues.en: The idea is really simple. It's just that you should minimize application state and minimize side effects.
cues.zh: 这个理念其实很简单。就是你应该最小化应用状态，最小化副作用。

cues.en: We don't need to go go to the extreme with it, but that's just the general guiding principles of React and I think that that idea is what feels rewarding to people.
cues.zh: 我们不需要走极端，但这正是 React 的总体指导原则，我认为正是这个理念让人们觉得有回报感。

cues.en: So people might not always express it like this,
cues.zh: 所以人们不一定总是这样表达，

cues.en: but, you know, they might say things like, I really like that React is composable. I feel like I can just stack my components together and it feels like I'm, you know, playing with building blocks basically.
cues.zh: 但他们可能会说，我真的很喜欢 React 的可组合性。感觉我可以直接把组件堆叠起来，就像在玩积木一样。

cues.en: Or they might say,
cues.zh: 或者他们可能会说，

cues.en: I really like that with React apps, my code is easier to reason about.
cues.zh: 我真的很喜欢用 React 应用时，我的代码更容易推理。

cues.en: Sounds like an opinion
cues.zh: 听起来像是一种主观看法

cues.en: and it's not really clear what people mean when they say reason about, but I think I have a pretty good idea what they're trying to say. When you can reason about something, it means that you can look at a small part of your code and you can understand a majority of the complexities and the interactions there without having to keep the whole entire program in your brain at once.
cues.zh: 而且人们说“推理”时到底是什么意思并不太清楚，但我想我大概明白他们想表达什么。当你能对某件事进行推理时，意味着你可以只看代码的一小部分，就能理解那里大部分的复杂性和交互，而不必把整个程序都同时装进脑子里。

cues.en: So it's easy to reason about.
cues.zh: 所以它很容易推理。

cues.en: Now building apps this way, the way that React encourages, minimizing side effects and state,
cues.zh: 现在用这种方式构建应用，也就是 React 鼓励的方式，尽量减少副作用和状态，

cues.en: That that makes your app easier to reason about and it sounds like an opinion but it's more than an opinion because it's also something that you can measure.
cues.zh: 这会让你的应用更容易推理，听起来像是一种主观看法，但它不只是看法，因为这也是可以衡量的。

cues.en: So take this example here.
cues.zh: 来看这个例子。

cues.en: This is a React component and it renders an array of friends and for each friend, it's going to render a div
cues.zh: 这是一个 React 组件，它渲染一个朋友数组，对于每个朋友，它会渲染一个 div

cues.en: and it's going print their name inside of that div but then it's going to wrap the whole thing in a container and we have an event handler on the outer container that says, whenever you click on anything in here, we're going to send a message to the user saying this is how many friends you have.
cues.zh: 然后在这个 div 里打印他们的名字，但接着它会把整个东西包在一个容器里，我们在外层容器上有一个事件处理器，说的是，每当你点击这里面任何东西时，我们就给用户发一条消息，说你有多少个朋友。

cues.en: But notice something interesting about this.
cues.zh: 但注意这里有个有趣的地方。

cues.en: Time can elapse between when you render that list initially
cues.zh: 从你最初渲染那个列表，

cues.en: and when that event handler occurs.
cues.zh: 到那个事件处理程序触发之间，可能经过一段时间。

cues.en: A lot can happen in that time.
cues.zh: 这期间可能发生很多事。

cues.en: What if somebody were to add an additional friend to that array? Just mutate it out from under you.
cues.zh: 如果有人往那个数组里再加一个好友呢？直接在你背后把它改了。

cues.en: I mean, they remove a friend.
cues.zh: 我是说，他们删掉了一个好友。

cues.en: Well, that message that you send to the user is going to be out of sync with the list that the user sees on the screen. That's mutation.
cues.zh: 那么你发给用户的消息，就会和用户屏幕上看到的列表不同步。这就是修改。

cues.en: Alright, so imagine you're in a really complicated
cues.zh: 好，想象你身处一个非常复杂的

cues.en: code base that's really big and uses lots of mutation everywhere.
cues.zh: 代码库中，它非常大，而且到处大量使用修改。

cues.en: Now imagine trying to go through, you know, in your head, look at this code and determine whether or not that mutation could happen.
cues.zh: 现在想象你在脑子里梳理这段代码，判断那种修改是否可能发生。

cues.en: Turns out it's really hard.
cues.zh: 结果发现这真的很难。

cues.en: So first of all, you have to go to every other module that calls into yours and you've got to confirm that after they pass that array to your component, they don't go and mutate that later.
cues.zh: 所以首先，你得去查看所有调用你模块的其他模块，并确认它们把那个数组传给你的组件后，不会再去修改它。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: That can be pretty time consuming,
cues.zh: 这可能相当耗时，

cues.en: but it's worse.
cues.zh: 但更糟的是。

cues.en: You also have to go find any other module that you're calling module passes that array to and confirm that they also don't mutate that array.
cues.zh: 你还得找到你调用、并把那个数组传进去的任何其他模块，确认它们也不会修改那个数组。

cues.en: That was... That's complicated and difficult for me to even explain so imagine trying to go through the actual code base and reason through that.
cues.zh: 这……这复杂到我自己都很难解释，所以想象一下真正去梳理实际代码库并推理这些。

cues.en: Alright. So contrast that with, if you know this array is not mutable, can never be mutated.
cues.zh: 好。那么对比一下这种情况：如果你知道这个数组不可变，永远不能被修改。

cues.en: Some language or type system, it won't even allow you to do it.
cues.zh: 有些语言或类型系统，根本不允许你这么做。

cues.en: The problem becomes
cues.zh: 问题就变得

cues.en: much simpler.
cues.zh: 简单多了。

cues.en: This is all you have to keep in your head to understand almost completely how this component works.
cues.zh: 你只需要在脑子里记住这些，就能几乎完全理解这个组件是怎么工作的。

cues.en: You could reason about it.
cues.zh: 你可以对它进行推理。

cues.en: So programming like this,
cues.zh: 所以这样编程，

cues.en: you know, it allows you to experience many small wins when you're programming. It's kinda like your brain gets this this
cues.zh: 你知道，它让你在编程时能体验到许多小的胜利。就像你的大脑时不时

cues.en: reward every so often and you're confident with what you've achieved. It makes programming fun. It's kinda like a game. I think that that's what people are talking about when they say, React made my job fun.
cues.zh: 得到一次奖励，你对自己所达成的东西充满信心。这让编程变得有趣。有点像玩游戏。我觉得这就是人们说“React 让我的工作变得有趣”时所指的意思。

cues.en: Okay. So React creates this pit of success where these kind of patterns, they're more easy, you know, they're easier to accomplish, they're more common.
cues.zh: 好。所以 React 创造了这样一个成功陷阱，让这类模式更容易，你知道，更容易达成，也更常见。

cues.en: That's what the pit of success means. You you just naturally fall into it.
cues.zh: 这就是成功陷阱的含义。你自然而然就会掉进去。

cues.en: Now a lot of purists might say, hey, I know the ways that you can circumvent these guardrails in React and I can make that array be mutated and that's true. But there's no denying that compared to the alternative paradigms in UI programming, it's a huge improvement and it was also a massive course correction for the direction that UI was heading in before React.
cues.zh: 现在很多纯粹主义者可能会说，嘿，我知道在 React 里怎么绕过这些护栏，我可以让那个数组被修改，这没错。但不可否认的是，与 UI 编程中的其他替代范式相比，这是一个巨大的改进，而且对 React 之前 UI 的发展方向来说，也是一次重大的纠偏。

cues.en: So React has become bigger than any library at this point.
cues.zh: 所以 React 在这一点上已经超越了一个库的范畴。

cues.en: It's really the idea of applying these timeless principles
cues.zh: 它真正代表的是把这些永恒的原则

cues.en: to the domain of UI programming.
cues.zh: 应用到 UI 编程领域。

cues.en: So it's interesting that
cues.zh: 有意思的是

cues.en: a lot of these ideas, they feel new to people, but they're not.
cues.zh: 这些想法对很多人来说很新鲜，但其实并不新。

cues.en: They're actually as old as computer science.
cues.zh: 它们其实和计算机科学一样古老。

cues.en: So it made me wonder, like, what else did we miss?
cues.zh: 所以我就想，我们还漏掉了什么？

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: What's in store for the future of UI programming?
cues.zh: UI 编程的未来会有什么？

cues.en: So in order to project out into the future, I think it's really helpful to take a look at the history of programming languages or at least the high level programming languages to see where some of these ideas originated from.
cues.zh: 所以为了展望未来，我觉得很有必要回顾一下编程语言的历史，至少是高级编程语言的历史，看看这些想法最早从哪里来。

cues.en: we're going way back. In 1932,
cues.zh: 我们要追溯得很远。1932 年，

cues.en: Alonso Church discovered Lambda calculus.
cues.zh: Alonso Church 发现了 Lambda 演算。

cues.en: So Lambda calculus is the simplest possible programming language you could imagine and its core construct is just a function with some lexical lexical scoping.
cues.zh: Lambda 演算能想象到的最简单的编程语言，它的核心构造就是一个带有词法作用域的函数。

cues.en: And really it turns out that from this really simple idea of just a function that takes a single argument, returns an expression,
cues.zh: 而事实证明，从这个非常简单的想法——一个函数接收单个参数、返回一个表达式，

cues.en: and then functions that you can apply, you can construct any computable program.
cues.zh: 再加上可以应用的函数，你就能构造出任何可计算的程序。

cues.en: That's interesting.
cues.zh: 这很有意思。

cues.en: So we're already starting to see the idea of computer programs being expressed
cues.zh: 我们已经开始看到这样一种想法：计算机程序被表达为

cues.en: as an expression that describes what the computer should do instead of actually just doing it in a sequence of imperative mutations.
cues.zh: 一个表达式，描述计算机应该做什么，而不是直接用一串命令式的修改去执行。

cues.en: This is really early.
cues.zh: 这非常早。

cues.en: What's really amazing here though is that Lambda calculus
cues.zh: 但真正令人惊叹的是，Lambda 演算

cues.en: was discovered before the first programmable computer was ever invented.
cues.zh: 是在第一台可编程计算机发明之前就被发现的了。

cues.en: So that should tell us something.
cues.zh: 这应该能告诉我们一些东西。

cues.en: So this wasn't contrived out of the constraints
cues.zh: 所以这并不是当时技术进步的种种限制所催生的

cues.en: of technological progress at the time.
cues.zh: 产物。

cues.en: These ideas, they seem to be timeless.
cues.zh: 这些思想似乎超越了时代。

cues.en: Alright. So it's not just mathematical theory though. In 1952, we see the invention of the Lisp programming language family and we're able to take which basically took later to calculus and made it human usable.
cues.zh: 好，所以这不仅仅是数学理论。1952 年，Lisp 编程语言家族被发明出来，我们基本上把后来的演算变成了人类可用的东西。

cues.en: And it's actually running on real hardware at that point.
cues.zh: 而且那时它已经在真实硬件上运行了。

cues.en: But then as time went on, more people developed and collaborated together. There's this increased increased demand for type systems and a way to automatically prove or, you know, reject bad programs ahead of time before you ship them.
cues.zh: 但随着时间推移，越来越多的人参与开发和协作。对类型系统的需求日益增长，需要一种能在发布之前自动证明或拒绝坏程序的方法。

cues.en: Sounds like a good idea to me.
cues.zh: 我觉得这主意不错。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: Roger Hindley and Robin Milner invented
cues.zh: Roger Hindley 和 Robin Milner 发明了

cues.en: the ML family of programming languages by creating the Hindley Milner type system.
cues.zh: ML 编程语言家族，通过创建 Hindley Milner 类型系统。

cues.en: So contrary to popular belief, ML does not stand for machine learning.
cues.zh: 与普遍看法相反，ML 并不代表机器学习。

cues.en: But what's really cool about ML is that it it really pioneered a really great
cues.zh: 但 ML 真正酷的地方在于，它开创了一个非常棒的

cues.en: type system where types weren't a burden.
cues.zh: 类型系统，类型不再是一种负担。

cues.en: You don't have to always write them so the compiler can infer them in most cases.
cues.zh: 你不必总是把它们写出来，所以在大多数情况下编译器可以推断出来。

cues.en: That's really great because a lot of type system skeptics might say, yeah, but static typing has all these benefits, but it's a huge burden. I have to always write them out everywhere. It ruins the rapid development.
cues.zh: 这真的很棒，因为很多对类型系统持怀疑态度的人可能会说，是啊，但静态类型有所有这些好处，却是个巨大的负担。我得处处都写出来。这破坏了快速开发。

cues.en: It's not so.
cues.zh: 并非如此。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: ML is like
cues.zh: ML 就像是

cues.en: the overall family of languages that Standard
cues.zh: 标准语言大家族

cues.en: ML, OCaml, and Elm
cues.zh: ML、OCaml 和 Elm

cues.en: all descend from.
cues.zh: 都源自的那个总体语言家族。

cues.en: So it looks like we're innovating at this really rapid pace here. Went from no computers even existing to
cues.zh: 看起来我们正以极快的速度在创新。从连计算机都还不存在，

cues.en: actually amazing type systems in like 40.
cues.zh: 到大概40年里就出现了令人惊叹的类型系统。

cues.en: So if you project out into the future, I mean, in forty years from now,
cues.zh: 所以如果你展望未来，我是说，从现在起四十年后，

cues.en: how amazing is it gonna be? I mean, everybody's gonna be using these awesome technologies. Right?
cues.zh: 那会有多厉害？我的意思是，大家都会用上这些牛逼的技术。对吧？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: apparently something had gone terribly wrong from 1973 to 2010 because when I started working as a web app developer, we weren't using all of these awesome paradigms. We weren't programming
cues.zh: 显然从1973年到2010年之间出了什么大问题，因为当我开始做Web应用开发者时，我们并没有用上这些很棒的范式。我们写代码时

cues.en: in patterns that were easy to reason about.
cues.zh: 用的不是那种容易推理的模式。

cues.en: We weren't even using static type systems at that at that time.
cues.zh: 那时候我们甚至都没用静态类型系统。

cues.en: And we were using actually two dynamic languages,
cues.zh: 而且我们用的其实是两门动态语言，

cues.en: JavaScript.
cues.zh: JavaScript。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: on top of that, one of them was PHP. So...
cues.zh: 更糟的是，其中一门还是PHP。所以……

cues.en: And we also had these like kinda kinda crazy
cues.zh: 我们还有那种有点疯的

cues.en: server setups where we would render this markup on the server, we'd send it across a wire, and we try to sprinkle some JavaScript on it on the client, you know, with the hopes of making the static document somewhat interactive.
cues.zh: 服务器配置，我们在服务器上渲染这些标记，通过网络发送出去，然后试着在客户端撒上一些JavaScript，你知道，希望能让这个静态文档有点交互性。

cues.en: You know,
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.zh: 所以我想，好吧，太好了。而且……反响的差别简直是天壤之别。大家都说，哇，这看起来很棒。那这个 React 到底是讲什么的？因为这样一来，我们就能越过最初这道坎，去聊真正重要的核心思想。

cues.zh: 有静摩擦力和动摩擦力。静摩擦力告诉你一开始要费多大力气才能把它推动，而动摩擦力告诉你……或者说石头已经在动的时候，你需要往系统里投入多少额外的能量才能让它继续动。

cues.zh: 于是你可能会想，哦对，这石头真不错。只要人们先推动初始阶段，你知道，之后他们就会看到它有多棒。

cues.zh: 所以你想让同事、项目贡献者加入进来。你想让他们快速上手。你想让他们看看你的项目并提交 pull request。

cues.zh: 这些就是让原生开发变得困难、缓慢或痛苦的一些因素。

cues.en: So what are we doing under the reason umbrella to improve things?
cues.zh: 那么我们在 Reason 这个大框架下做了些什么来改进呢？

cues.en: Well, if we want to get web developers on board with the native development workflows,
cues.zh: 如果我们想让 Web 开发者接受原生开发工作流，

cues.en: we need something that's familiar. It's gotta be one click.
cues.zh: 就需要一些他们熟悉的东西。必须是一键式的。

cues.en: We need something that's easy.
cues.zh: 需要简单易用。

cues.en: So Andre Pop has been building something called easy.
cues.zh: 于是 Andre Pop 开发了一个叫 easy 的工具。

cues.en: Easy is a... Is like the one easy button that you need to press to automate to speed up
cues.zh: Easy 就像是那个你只需按一下的简单按钮，用来自动化、加速

cues.en: and perform native builds.
cues.zh: 并执行原生构建。

cues.en: It feels just like NPM package management also, actually.
cues.zh: 实际上，它感觉很像 NPM 包管理。

cues.en: You got a package JSON. You specify your dependencies.
cues.zh: 你有一个 package JSON，指定你的依赖。

cues.en: So really any web developer can just get started really quickly. They immediately know how to navigate the project.
cues.zh: 所以任何 Web 开发者都能很快上手，他们立刻就知道如何浏览项目。

cues.en: But it's not NPM. It doesn't use NPM. It doesn't use Yarn.
cues.zh: 但它不是 NPM，不使用 NPM，也不使用 Yarn。

cues.en: It's a complete reimplementation of a package management workflow.
cues.zh: 它是对包管理工作流的完全重新实现。

cues.en: And it's implemented in Reason native itself, so it's also really fast.
cues.zh: 而且它是用 Reason native 本身实现的，所以也非常快。

cues.en: It's really easy to use. You just type ESY in the command line when you're in a project, and it'll just do everything.
cues.zh: 它非常易用。在项目里只需在命令行输入 ESY，它就会搞定一切。

cues.en: It'll build, install dependencies.
cues.zh: 它会构建、安装依赖。

cues.en: It's actually pretty incredible what's happening there. I think of it as like a React but for package management. So in the same way that we're bringing the ideas of React to the language of reason, we're bringing the ideas of React to the package management with EZ.
cues.zh: 那里发生的事情其实相当不可思议。我觉得它就像是包管理领域的 React。就像我们把 React 的理念带到 Reason 语言中一样，我们也通过 EZ 把 React 的理念带到了包管理中。

cues.en: So when you run EZ, it reconciles your project,
cues.zh: 当你运行 EZ 时，它会协调你的项目，

cues.en: fetches what needs to be fetched from the network, builds what needs to be built,
cues.zh: 从网络获取需要获取的内容，构建需要构建的内容，

cues.en: and does it really fast.
cues.zh: 而且速度非常快。

cues.en: But what's really cool is that it also caches those builds for your project independencies
cues.zh: 但真正酷的是，它还会跨你所有的项目，为你的项目依赖缓存这些构建结果。

cues.en: across all your projects. So the more you use it, the faster it gets when you're when you're developing native.
cues.zh: 所以用得越多，在开发原生应用时它就越快。

cues.en: It uses some code from OCaml's package manager opam and also has integration with opam so that it can consume those packages and build them, and it's really standing on the shoulders of giants here with both OCaml and opam and a lot of the research that went in there, including some of the Windows support.
cues.zh: 它使用了 OCaml 包管理器 opam 的一些代码，并且与 opam 集成，能够消费这些包并构建它们；它真正是站在巨人的肩膀上，依托 OCaml、opam 以及其中投入的大量研究，包括一些 Windows 支持。

cues.en: But it also supports native c programs and c plus plus libraries.
cues.zh: 但它也支持原生 C 程序和 C++ 库。

cues.en: It also supports JavaScript packages. So it's really kind of one tool chain that can can do it all there.
cues.zh: 它还支持 JavaScript 包。所以它确实是一种能搞定这一切的工具链。

cues.en: So Reason takes the ideas of React to the next level.
cues.zh: Reason 把 React 的理念提升到了下一个层次。

cues.en: And I see it as a way to unlock your potential as a developer
cues.zh: 我把它看作释放你作为开发者潜能的一种方式，

cues.en: because it allows you to learn one language that improves the user experience
cues.zh: 因为它让你学习一门语言就能改善用户体验，

cues.en: across a wide variety of use cases and constraints.
cues.zh: 覆盖广泛的使用场景和约束条件。

cues.en: So I want to leave you with one question.
cues.zh: 所以我想留给你们一个问题。

cues.en: What could you build with Reason?
cues.zh: 你能用 Reason 构建什么？

cues.en: Maybe you could build a really cool data fetching paradigm or framework that runs everywhere.
cues.zh: 也许你可以构建一个非常酷的、能在任何地方运行的数据获取范式或框架。

cues.en: Maybe you could build a new UI library.
cues.zh: 也许你可以构建一个新的 UI 库。

cues.en: Maybe you could build what comes after React.
cues.zh: 也许你可以构建 React 之后的东西。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家。
